# How often should you clean a fish tank, and how do you never forget it?

URL: https://guledaaydemir.github.io/PETO/guides/fish-tank-cleaning-schedule-reminder/

**Quick answer:** Most fish and turtle care guides recommend regular partial water changes, often weekly, plus rinsing the filter media lightly in old tank water rather than under the tap, so the helpful bacteria survive. The right interval for your tank depends on its size, how many animals live in it, how much you feed and the filter, so ask your aquarium shop or vet and then keep to it. PETO’s free aquarium care turns that interval into an “every N days” reminder (2 to 60 days) counted from the day you actually cleaned, and logs the % of water changed and whether the filter was cleaned.

Key points:
- Partial water changes dilute the waste a filter can’t break down; the filter needs care too, but over-cleaning it removes helpful bacteria.
- Rinse filter media lightly in tank water you’ve removed, not under the tap: chlorine or chloramine in tap water can kill the helpful bacteria.
- The right interval depends on your tank, how many animals live in it, feeding and the filter; your aquarium shop or vet can help you set it.
- Overfeeding fouls the water: uneaten food rots, and turtles in particular produce a lot of waste.
- In PETO, aquarium care is free for fish and turtles: an every-N-days cleaning routine counted from the last real clean, an “Aquarium” card and feeding reminders.

## How often should you clean a fish tank?

There isn’t one interval that fits every tank, but care guides agree on the method: small, regular **partial water changes** and gentle care of the filter. For goldfish, RSPCA Australia suggests weekly partial water changes of 10 to 25% of the water together with a gravel clean, and the Ornamental Aquatic Trade Association (OATA) recommends a partial change at least once a week. For terrapins such as red-eared sliders, the RSPCA suggests weekly partial changes too.

Treat those figures as a starting point, not as a rule for your tank. How often your tank needs attention depends on its size, how many fish or turtles live in it, how much you feed and the filter you use. Ask your aquarium shop or vet to help you set your interval. The RSPCA recommends buying from a reputable aquatics retailer who will advise you, and OATA says: if in doubt, ask. Then turn the answer into a routine you can actually keep.

## Why partial water changes and filter care matter

Fish and turtles live in their own waste. Uneaten food and droppings break down in the water, and the filter is home to helpful bacteria that break down waste such as ammonia. Without those bacteria, waste builds up and, as RSPCA Australia warns, can kill fish. Partial water changes dilute the waste the filter can’t break down; that’s exactly how the RSPCA explains them for terrapin tanks. A gravel siphon lifts droppings and leftover food out of the substrate while you change the water.

The filter needs care, but not too much. RSPCA Australia says not to clean the filter with tap water, and OATA explains why: chlorine or chloramine in tap water may kill the helpful bacteria. Instead, rinse the media lightly in the tank water you’ve just taken out. RSPCA Australia also warns that over-cleaning the filter media removes those bacteria. And treat the new water with a tap water conditioner (dechlorinator) before it goes in.

## What decides the right interval for your tank?

- **Tank size.** A small volume of water has less room to dilute waste.

- **Stocking.** More fish, or a bigger turtle, means more waste.

- **Feeding.** Uneaten food rots and fouls the water. RSPCA Australia calls overfeeding the most common problem with goldfish, and the RSPCA names over-feeding as the main cause of poor water quality in terrapin tanks.

- **Filter.** The type and capacity of the filter change how much work is left for you.

- **A new tank.** New tanks need closer checks while the helpful bacteria settle in; the RSPCA recommends fishless cycling when you set one up.

Water test kits show how your tank is coping. OATA advises setting a routine for testing and recording your results, so you spot changes quickly. If you’re not sure what a reading means, take it to your aquarium shop. PETO doesn’t give water-chemistry advice: the schedule is yours, set with someone who knows your tank.

## Turtle tanks: more waste, same idea

Turtles are messy. The RSPCA says red-eared sliders produce lots of waste, so their water needs powerful filtration and regular maintenance. The basics are the same: weekly partial water changes, swishing the filter sponge in tank water rather than under the tap, and not overfeeding. The RSPCA also recommends registering with a reptile vet, so you have someone to ask when something looks wrong. Whatever the tank, wash your hands when you’re done.

## A simple tank-cleaning routine you can keep

- Prepare the replacement water and treat it with a conditioner, as your shop recommends.

- Siphon out part of the water, cleaning the gravel or sand as you go.

- If the filter needs it, rinse the media lightly in the water you removed.

- Top up with the treated water.

- Write down what you did: roughly what percentage of the water you changed, and whether you cleaned the filter.

The last step is the one most people skip, and it’s the one that makes the next clean easy to plan. “Did we change the water last weekend or the one before?” has a real answer when it’s written down.

## How to set an aquarium cleaning reminder in PETO

PETO’s aquarium care is free for fish and turtles. When you add a fish, PETO suggests a feeding and an aquarium routine; for a turtle, feeding, attention and aquarium. They’re only suggestions: keep, change or remove them.

- **Every N days.** Set the aquarium routine to repeat every N days, from 2 to 60, using the interval you agreed with your shop or vet. It’s counted from the day the clean was actually done, so if you clean a day late and log it, the next reminder moves too.

- **Time and “Remind me”.** Pick a time when you usually have half an hour free, and get the reminder at that time, 10 minutes before or 30 minutes before.

- **Log the clean.** Record the % of water changed and whether the filter was cleaned.

- **Act on the reminder.** Mark it done, “Snooze 15 min” or “Skip” right from the notification.

The **“Aquarium”** card on your fish’s or turtle’s page shows the last clean and the next date, with a short reminder of how it works: “Counted from the last clean: log it a day late and the next reminder moves too.”

(Screenshot: Bubbles the fish: the pet page with the “Aquarium” card showing the last clean and the next date.)

Feeding works like any other routine: one or more feeding times, a default portion if you like, and one-tap logging. Since overfeeding fouls the water, a shared record of who already fed the fish is worth having in a busy home.

(Screenshot: The routine editor, shown here for Buddy’s feeding: times, Repeat, “Remind me” and the reminder switch. The aquarium routine uses the same editor.)

> Tip: Log the clean **before you put the bucket away**. The next date counts from your log, so logging right away keeps the reminder in step with your tank, not with the plan.

## See the schedule and share the job

The **Calendar** shows the month with coloured dots per care type, and you can filter it by pet. If the whole household looks after the tank, Family sharing (Premium to create, free to join) lets everyone see who fed, walked or played, so the fish don’t get a second breakfast. Going away? The free pet-sitter care card gives your neighbour the routines, times, notes and a phone number on one page. New to PETO? Start with the quick-start guide, and see the daily routine guide for how routines fit together.

(Screenshot: The Calendar: a month grid with coloured dots per care type and a pet filter.)

Your pet data is saved on your device, with no PETO account and no ads. And PETO isn’t a vet or an aquarium expert: if your fish or turtle seems unwell, ask your vet.

## Questions people ask

**How often should I clean my fish tank?** It depends on the tank’s size, how many fish live in it, how much you feed and the filter. Care guides for goldfish from RSPCA Australia and OATA recommend a partial water change about once a week, with a gravel clean. Ask your aquarium shop or vet what suits your tank, then keep to that interval.

**Can I rinse the aquarium filter under the tap?** Care guides advise against it: chlorine or chloramine in tap water may kill the helpful bacteria in the filter. Rinse the media lightly in tank water you’ve removed during a water change, and don’t over-clean it.

**How often should a turtle tank be cleaned?** Turtles such as red-eared sliders produce a lot of waste, so their tanks need powerful filtration and regular maintenance. The RSPCA suggests weekly partial water changes for terrapins. Ask a reptile vet about your own setup.

**How does PETO count the next cleaning date?** From the day you actually log the clean. You set the aquarium routine to repeat every N days (2 to 60); if you clean and log it a day late, the next reminder moves by a day too. The Aquarium card shows the last clean and the next date.

**Is PETO’s aquarium care free, and does it give water advice?** Aquarium care is free for fish and turtles: the every-N-days cleaning routine, logging the % of water changed and filter cleaning, the Aquarium card and feeding reminders. PETO doesn’t give water-chemistry advice; ask your aquarium shop or vet.

Sources:
- RSPCA Australia (2024). How should I care for my goldfish? https://kb.rspca.org.au/knowledge-base/how-should-i-care-for-my-goldfish/
- OATA (n.d.). How to look after goldfish in an aquarium / fish tank. https://ornamentalfish.org/what-we-do/advice-information/care-sheets/caresheets-coldwater-fish/how-to-look-after-goldfish-in-an-aquarium-fishtank/
- RSPCA (n.d.). How to care for a terrapin. https://www.rspca.org.uk/adviceandwelfare/pets/other/terrapin
- RSPCA (n.d.). Keeping fish as pets. https://www.rspca.org.uk/adviceandwelfare/pets/fish

# How to make your pet's bark or meow your iPhone reminder sound

URL: https://guledaaydemir.github.io/PETO/guides/pet-voice-notification-sound/

**Quick answer:** In PETO, open Settings → Notifications → “Pet voices”, check that “Reminders in my pet's voice” is on and tap “Record” next to your pet to capture up to 8 seconds of its bark, meow or chirp. PETO trims the silence and evens out the loudness, and from then on that pet's reminders, follow-ups and nudges play its own voice instead of the default sound. Tap “Test” to get a real reminder in about 3 seconds; the feature is free and the recording stays on your device.

Key points:
- Settings → Notifications → “Pet voices” → “Record”: up to 8 seconds per pet.
- Each pet's reminders, follow-ups and nudges play that pet's own voice.
- Tap “Test” for a real reminder in about 3 seconds, then lock your phone to hear it.
- Silent mode, a Focus or notifications switched off can keep it quiet.
- It's free; the microphone is used only while recording and the clip stays on your device.

## Can your pet's bark or meow be your iPhone reminder sound?

Yes. PETO, a pet-care routine app for iPhone, iPad and Mac that is free to download, lets you record your pet's bark, meow or chirp and use it as the notification sound for that pet's reminders. Open **Settings → Notifications → "Pet voices"**, make sure **"Reminders in my pet's voice"** is on and tap **"Record"** next to your pet. From then on, that pet's reminders, follow-ups and nudges play its own voice instead of the default sound.

It's free, it works per pet, and the recording stays on your device. Here's how to set it up, record a clean clip and fix it when you can't hear it.

## Why a familiar sound is easier to notice

Phones chime, ping and buzz all day, and a standard alert sounds like every other app. That makes it easy to swipe away without reading. A sound you know well is different: you recognise it before you look at the screen, and you know straight away which pet the reminder is about.

That helps with the jobs that slip on a busy day, like the evening meal, the afternoon walk or ten minutes of play. Hearing your dog's bark at dinner time feels more like a friendly nudge than a beep. It won't turn anyone into a perfect pet parent, but it makes the reminder harder to miss and a little more fun.

## How to set up pet voice reminders in PETO, step by step

- Open PETO and go to **Settings → Notifications → "Pet voices"**.

- Check that **"Reminders in my pet's voice"** is switched on.

- Find your pet in the list and tap **"Record"**. PETO needs microphone access to record, so allow it when your iPhone asks.

- When your pet has made its sound, tap **"Stop & save"**. You have up to 8 seconds. PETO trims the silence and evens out the loudness, so there's nothing to edit.

- Tap **"Play"** to listen back. Not happy with it? Tap **"Re-record"**.

- Tap **"Test"**. PETO sends a real reminder in about 3 seconds. As the app suggests, lock your phone to hear it like the real thing.

Changed your mind? Tap the bin icon next to the recording and confirm, and that pet's reminders go back to the default sound. You can record a new clip whenever you like.

(Screenshot: "Pet voices": switch on "Reminders in my pet's voice" and tap Record next to each pet.)

## Give every pet its own reminder voice

Pet voices work per pet, which is where they shine in a busy household. Record the dog's bark, the cat's meow and the budgie's chirp separately. Each pet's reminders, follow-ups and smart nudges then play that pet's own clip, while a pet without a recording simply keeps the default sound. A quiet rabbit like Poppy may be happy with the default anyway.

The result: when your phone barks, it's about the dog; when it meows, it's the cat's turn, and you can tell from the next room. PETO already groups reminders per pet and shows the pet's pixel sprite, so the sound and the picture match. You can still act right from the notification with "Fed ✓", "Snooze 15 min" or "Skip".

Haven't set up any times yet? The daily routine guide explains routines and "Remind me", and the quick-start guide gets you going.

(Screenshot: Buddy, Milo and Poppy on Home. Each pet can have its own reminder voice.)

## Tips for recording a clear bark, meow or chirp

- **Pick a quiet room.** Turn off the TV, the washing machine and the cooker hood. Background noise ends up in the clip too.

- **Hold the phone fairly close**, without pushing it into your pet's face.

- **Catch a natural moment.** Many dogs bark when the doorbell rings or the lead comes out, many cats meow around mealtimes, and many birds chirp in the morning. Start recording just before; the silence is trimmed anyway.

- **Try a treat or a favourite toy** if your pet "talks" when it wants something. If your dog knows a "speak" cue, use it.

- **Keep it short and happy.** One clear bark or meow is plenty; you don't need all 8 seconds. A cheerful sound makes a nicer reminder than an anxious one.

- **Never frighten or tease your pet** to get a sound. If it isn't in the mood, try another day.

> Tip: Your pet will hear the reminders too, and some pets may prick up their ears or answer back. If yours seems unsettled by its own voice coming from the phone, record a softer sound or delete the clip to go back to the **default sound**.

## Why can't I hear my pet's voice? What to check

If the test or a real reminder stays silent, one of these is usually the reason. PETO points out several of them on the "Pet voices" screen.

- **Notifications are off for PETO.** PETO tells you: "Notifications are off for PETO, so the test can't play." In the iPhone Settings app, go to Notifications → PETO and turn on Allow Notifications, plus Sounds if you see it. Also check the notifications master switch in PETO's own Settings.

- **Silent mode is on.** As the screen notes, your iPhone's ring/silent switch still applies. In Silent mode, iPhone doesn't play alerts or sound effects, though it may still vibrate. Depending on your model, turn it off with the Ring/Silent switch, the Action button, Control Center or Settings → Sounds & Haptics.

- **A Focus is on.** Do Not Disturb, Sleep or another Focus can silence notifications. In Settings → Focus, choose the Focus, tap Apps and add PETO to the apps allowed to notify you. PETO's feeding, walk, medication and vet reminders are time-sensitive, and Apple explains that turning on Time Sensitive Notifications for a Focus lets apps send those immediately.

- **Microphone access is off.** If you can't record, PETO shows "Microphone access is off" with a button that opens Settings. You can also go to Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone and turn PETO on.

- **The volume is low or the clip is faint.** Turn up the ringer and alerts volume, and re-record closer to your pet if the clip sounds quiet.

(Screenshot: PETO's Settings: care-reminder switches and notification settings.)

## Is my pet's recording private?

Yes. PETO uses the microphone only while you record a pet voice, and the recording stays on your device. PETO has no account and no server of its own; your pets' profiles, routines and logs are saved on the device too.

PETO does collect anonymous usage statistics, such as which screens open and which features are used. They never include pet names, notes or photos, and your recording stays on the phone. You can turn the statistics off in Settings → Data → "Share anonymous usage stats". To remove a voice, delete the recording; Settings → Reset all data, or deleting the app, removes everything PETO stored on the device.

## Pet voice reminder checklist

- [ ] Open Settings → Notifications → Pet voices in PETO
- [ ] Check that "Reminders in my pet's voice" is on
- [ ] Record each pet in a quiet room with the phone close
- [ ] Play it back and re-record if it sounds faint
- [ ] Tap Test and lock your phone to hear it
- [ ] Turn off Silent mode or allow PETO in your Focus
- [ ] Delete a clip any time to go back to the default sound

Want more of your pet in the app? Dress your pixel pet up for Halloween, New Year and Bayram, and press and hold it to give it a pat.

## Questions people ask

**Can I use my dog's bark as a notification sound on iPhone?** Yes, for PETO's reminders. In PETO, go to Settings → Notifications → “Pet voices” and record up to 8 seconds of your dog's bark. That dog's reminders, follow-ups and nudges then play it instead of the default sound. Sounds from other apps don't change.

**Is the pet voice feature in PETO free?** Yes. Pet voices are free, like PETO's core reminders and logging. Optional PETO Premium, sold as monthly, yearly or lifetime, adds extras such as medication routines and seasonal outfits.

**Why can't I hear my pet's voice when a PETO reminder arrives?** Check that notifications are allowed for PETO, that Silent mode is off (in Silent mode iPhone doesn't play alert sounds, though it may vibrate) and that no Focus is silencing PETO. Then tap “Test” in Pet voices and lock your phone to hear it.

**Can each of my pets have its own reminder sound?** Yes. Recordings are per pet, so the dog's reminders can bark and the cat's can meow. A pet without a recording keeps the default sound.

**Does PETO upload my pet's recording?** No. PETO uses the microphone only while you record, and the recording stays on your device. PETO has no account or server of its own; its anonymous usage statistics don't include the recording and can be turned off in Settings → Data.

Sources:
- Apple Support (n.d.). Change notification settings on iPhone. https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/change-notification-settings-iph7c3d96bab/ios
- Apple Support (n.d.). Silence iPhone. https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/silence-iphone-iph81c7fd7d1/ios
- Apple Support (n.d.). Allow or silence notifications for a Focus on iPhone. https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/allow-or-silence-notifications-for-a-focus-iph21d43af5b/ios
- Apple Support (n.d.). Control access to hardware features on iPhone. https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/control-access-to-hardware-features-iph168c4bbd5/ios

# When your pet dies: what to do with the reminders, the records and the memories

URL: https://guledaaydemir.github.io/PETO/guides/when-your-pet-dies-memorial-mode/

**Quick answer:** When your pet dies, you don’t have to delete the app or any of their records; the one thing worth doing soon is stopping the reminders. In PETO, memorial mode (free, never behind Premium) quietly stops every reminder, nudge, Live Activity and Apple Watch entry for that pet, keeps all logs, photos and the health record, and turns the pet’s page into a simple memorial you can share. It’s under Edit Pet → Memorial mode → “Create memorial”, and you can leave it at any time.

Key points:
- You don’t need to delete anything when your pet dies; stopping the reminders is the one thing worth doing soon.
- PETO’s memorial mode is free and never behind Premium: Edit Pet → Memorial mode → “Create memorial”.
- Every reminder, nudge, Live Activity and Apple Watch entry for that pet stops quietly; logs, photos and the health record are kept.
- The memorial page shows dates, years of love, a few words, memories together from the log and a shareable memorial card.
- Memorial mode can be undone at any time, and free pet-loss support lines are there when you want to talk.

## What should you do with your pet’s app when your pet dies?

Nothing has to happen today: you don’t need to delete the app, the photos or the years of records. The one thing worth doing soon is stopping the reminders, because a notification about feeding a pet who has died can catch you off guard on an ordinary morning.

In PETO, **memorial mode** does exactly that. It’s free for everyone and never behind Premium. Every reminder for that pet stops quietly, everything you logged is kept, and the pet’s page becomes a simple memorial. This guide explains how it works, what to tell the people who shared the care, and where to find support when the grief is heavy.

## Why reminders that keep arriving hurt

A care app is meant to be persistent. While your pet is alive, that’s the point: a reminder at 7:30 every morning, a gentle follow-up when a walk isn’t logged, a playtime countdown on the Lock Screen. After a death, the same persistence lands differently. A “Meal time” alert or a nudge saying your pet misses you can arrive in a meeting or on the first quiet morning, and each one brings the loss back at a moment you didn’t choose.

The American Veterinary Medical Association writes about how loud the silence at home can feel after a pet dies. A reminder breaks into that silence without warning. Stopping the reminders isn’t forgetting. It simply lets you choose when to think about your pet, and how.

## How to turn on memorial mode in PETO

Memorial mode lives where you edit your pet’s profile:

- Open your pet’s page and choose **Edit Pet**.

- Tap **Memorial mode**. A short sheet opens with the words “We’re so sorry. [Name] was deeply loved.” and explains what will happen.

- Check the date, add **a few words** if you like (they’re optional) and tap **“Create memorial”**, or “Not now” if you aren’t ready.

(Screenshot: The memorial sheet: “We’re so sorry” with your pet’s name, what happens next, the date, “A few words (optional)” and “Create memorial”.)

From that moment, every reminder, nudge, Live Activity and Apple Watch entry for that pet stops quietly. There’s no farewell notification and nothing to dismiss. Your other pets’ routines carry on as before. If you had recorded your pet’s bark or meow for reminders in their own voice, those reminders stop too, so the recording won’t play unexpectedly as a notification sound.

And nothing is final: you can leave memorial mode at any time, and the reminders resume.

## What the memorial page shows

Instead of a list of jobs, the pet’s page becomes a quiet memorial page. It holds:

- **Dates** and **years of love**: the time you had together.

- **A few words** you write yourself, such as “Forever our little sunshine”.

- **Memories together**, drawn from your own log: walks together, meals shared, play sessions and a favourite park.

- A **shareable memorial card** (“Share memorial”) to send to family and friends.

The pixel pet is drawn still, without the everyday animations. The few words can be as short as you like. Some people write a nickname, others a line that only the family understands.

(Screenshot: Buddy’s “In memory” page: the dates, “3 years of love”, memories together (7 walks, 13 meals shared, 6 play sessions, a favourite park) and “Share memorial”.)

## Logs, photos and the health record are all kept

Memorial mode doesn’t delete anything. Every log, every photo and the whole health record stay on your device as they were. That can matter in a few ways:

- **Memories.** The log turns out to be a diary you didn’t know you were keeping: walks, park visits, evenings of cuddles.

- **Questions later.** If you want to talk through the last months with your vet, the vaccines and the weight log are still there to look at.

- **Future pets.** One day, perhaps not soon, the record may help you remember which food suited, which routine worked and what you would do again.

The health record guide explains what the record holds.

(Screenshot: The health record, with vaccines and weight, stays as it was.)

## What to tell family members who shared the care

If others helped with meals and walks, they should hear the news from you, not from a reminder that suddenly goes quiet. That includes a partner, children, flatmates and anyone you share the care with through Family sharing. A few things worth saying:

- **That you’re creating a memorial**, so the silence that follows makes sense to them.

- **What changes:** the reminders and nudges for this pet stop; the logs, photos and health record are kept; and everything can be undone.

- **That they can help with the few words**, if that feels right. Children often want to add something of their own; the RSPCA’s pet bereavement toolkit has a page on children and pet loss.

Remember people outside the home too: a sitter, a dog walker or a neighbour who looked after your pet. A short message, or the memorial card, lets them know.

(Screenshot: Buddy’s Care Plan: every routine has its own reminder switch, if you’d rather pause reminders before creating a memorial.)

> Tip: There’s no deadline. If creating a memorial feels too soon, you can turn off the reminder switch on each of the pet’s routines for now and come back to memorial mode later. Memorial mode is the one step that stops everything for that pet at once.

## Gentle ways to remember your pet

There’s no right way to remember, and no schedule for grief. A few ideas people find helpful:

- **Write a few words.** The AVMA suggests writing a tribute or a letter to your pet as a way to keep memories close. The memorial page has room for a short one.

- **Share the memorial card** with the people who knew your pet: family, the sitter, the neighbour who always said hello.

- **Look back through the log** when you feel ready. “Memories together” brings out moments like a favourite park.

- **Visit a place you shared.** The RSPCA lists favourite walks and places among the ways people remember.

- **Keep the health record** for the day another animal joins your home. The RSPCA calls that a personal decision with no fixed timing.

## Where to find support after your pet dies

Grief for a pet is real grief, yet in an RSPCA survey more than half of the people who answered said they felt they had to hide it. Talking to someone who understands can help. These free services are run by animal charities and a veterinary college:

- **Blue Cross Pet Loss Support** (UK, formerly the Pet Bereavement Support Service): free, confidential support from trained volunteers on 0800 096 6606, 8.30am to 8.30pm every day, or by email.

- **Cats Protection’s Paws to Listen** (UK): a free, confidential phone line, 0800 024 94 94, on weekdays.

- **Cornell Pet Loss Support Hotline** (US): 607-218-7457, answered by veterinary student volunteers trained with professional grief counsellors. Hours vary, so check the website.

- **RSPCA pet bereavement toolkit** (UK): guidance on coping, children and pet loss, and supporting someone who is grieving.

- **AVMA: Coping with the loss of a pet** (US): a short, kind read.

These lines offer a listening ear, not counselling. If grief feels overwhelming or you’re struggling to cope, please reach out to your doctor or a mental health professional.

Memorial mode is free for everyone, with or without Premium. If PETO was part of your pet’s everyday life, it can also hold their memory, quietly.

## Questions people ask

**What happens to reminders when I turn on memorial mode?** Every reminder, nudge, Live Activity and Apple Watch entry for that pet stops quietly, with no farewell notification. Reminders for your other pets carry on as before.

**Does memorial mode delete my pet’s data?** No. Every log, photo and the full health record are kept on your device. The pet’s page becomes a memorial page with dates, years of love, a few words you write, memories together from the log and a shareable memorial card.

**Is PETO’s memorial mode free?** Yes. Memorial mode is free for everyone and never behind Premium. You’ll find it under Edit Pet → Memorial mode → “Create memorial”.

**Can I undo memorial mode?** Yes. You can leave memorial mode at any time, and the pet’s reminders resume. Nothing is deleted while the memorial is in place.

**Where can I find support after my pet dies?** Free options include Blue Cross Pet Loss Support in the UK (0800 096 6606, every day), Cats Protection’s Paws to Listen in the UK and the Cornell Pet Loss Support Hotline in the US. They offer a listening ear, not counselling; if grief feels overwhelming, talk to your doctor or a mental health professional.

Sources:
- Blue Cross (2020). Pet loss. https://www.bluecross.org.uk/pet-loss
- Cats Protection (n.d.). Grief and loss. https://www.cats.org.uk/what-we-do/grief
- Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine (n.d.). Pet Loss Resources and Support. https://www.vet.cornell.edu/about-us/outreach/pet-loss-support-hotline
- RSPCA (2026). Pet bereavement toolkit. https://www.rspca.org.uk/adviceandwelfare/pets/bereavement
- RSPCA (2026). How to cope with the loss of a pet. https://www.rspca.org.uk/adviceandwelfare/pets/bereavement/coping
- AVMA (n.d.). Coping with the loss of a pet. https://www.avma.org/resources-tools/pet-owners/petcare/coping-loss-pet

# Halloween, New Year and Bayram outfits for your pixel pet (and how it comes alive)

URL: https://guledaaydemir.github.io/PETO/guides/pet-halloween-new-year-bayram-outfits/

**Quick answer:** PETO, a pet-care routine app for iPhone and iPad, has pixel outfits for your pet's avatar: a witch hat or pumpkin cap for Halloween, a Santa hat, reindeer antlers or party hat for New Year, and a fez, crescent tiara or tulip crown for Bayram (the Turkish name for Eid). Anyone can try them on for free; keeping one on your pet is Premium. The pixel pet is also “alive” for free: press and hold to pet it, and it sleeps in a nightcap at night, yawns awake in the morning and walks around on muddy paws after a walk.

Key points:
- Eight pixel outfits across three seasons: Halloween, New Year and Bayram.
- The live season is featured; released outfits stay wearable all year.
- Try any outfit on for free; keeping one on your pet is Premium.
- The living pet is free: press and hold to pet it, with haptics.
- Dressing up your real pet? Only if it's relaxed, only briefly, and never unattended.

## How do you dress up your pet in PETO?

Open your pet, go to **Edit Pet** and tap **"Outfits"**. The picker shows your pet's pixel avatar with seasonal headwear for **Halloween**, **New Year** and **Bayram**. Tap any outfit to try it on in the preview. Trying on is free for everyone; keeping an outfit on your pet is part of PETO Premium.

- Open your pet and go to Edit Pet.

- Tap "Outfits".

- Tap an outfit to see it on your pet, or "No outfit" for the plain look.

- With Premium, tap "Done" to keep it. Without Premium, the button reads "Unlock with Premium".

The outfits are pixel headwear drawn on top of the avatar, so they fit every one of PETO's 104 pixel pets, whether yours is a golden retriever, a tuxedo cat, a white rabbit or a leopard gecko. Your routines don't change at all; your pet just looks festive while you do them.

(Screenshot: The outfit picker: try Halloween, New Year and Bayram headwear on for free; keeping one is Premium.)

## Every seasonal outfit in PETO, and when each season is featured

| Season | Featured in PETO | Outfits |

| Halloween | 1 October – 7 November | Witch hat, pumpkin cap |

| New Year | 1 December – 15 January | Santa hat, reindeer antlers, party hat |

| Bayram | From a week before Ramazan Bayramı and Kurban Bayramı | Fez, crescent tiara, tulip crown |

The season that's live is featured in the picker. Outside those dates nothing disappears: released outfits stay wearable all year, so a pumpkin cap in March is entirely up to you.

## What is Bayram, and how does PETO know the dates?

Bayram is the Turkish word for a holiday or festival. In Türkiye the two big religious ones are **Ramazan Bayramı**, the Turkish name for Eid al-Fitr at the end of Ramadan, and **Kurban Bayramı**, the Turkish name for Eid al-Adha. They're family days: people visit relatives, greet their elders and share sweets, which is why Ramazan Bayramı is also called Şeker Bayramı, the "sugar feast".

Both follow the lunar Islamic calendar, so in the Gregorian calendar they move about 11 days earlier every year. PETO works the dates out with the Umm al-Qura calendar and features the Bayram outfits from a week before each Bayram, so you don't have to look anything up. The fez, crescent tiara and tulip crown nod to Turkish style; the tulip, for instance, is a classic motif in İznik tiles.

## Try outfits on for free, keep one with Premium

Trying on is open to everyone, with or without Premium, so you can see your dog in reindeer antlers before deciding anything. In the picker, each season carries a Premium badge and the outfits show small locks; they're about keeping an outfit, not trying it on.

PETO Premium is optional and sold as monthly, yearly (both renew until cancelled in your Apple ID subscriptions) or lifetime, a one-time purchase that never renews. Apple handles the purchase, and with Universal Purchase one Premium unlocks PETO on iPhone, iPad and Mac. Premium also covers things like creating family sharing, medication routines and the vet PDF report. Core reminders, logging and the living pet below stay free.

## Meet the living pet: pet it, watch it sleep, spot the muddy paws

Outfits are the seasonal part. The everyday part is free: on Home and on the pet page, your pixel pet is "alive".

- **Press and hold to pet it.** A dog wags, a cat or small furry pet purrs, birds and fish flutter, and reptiles nuzzle. You feel it through haptics, and it's mirrored on Apple Watch.

- **Bedtime and wake-up.** At night your pet sleeps in a nightcap under a moon. The first time you look each morning, it yawns awake with a sun.

- **Muddy paws.** Right after you log a walk, your pet wanders about on muddy paws for a while. Tracking walks on your wrist? See Apple Watch walks.

With Reduce Motion turned on, the looks stay but the movement stops. A pet in memorial mode is drawn still.

(Screenshot: Buddy's page: press and hold the pixel pet to pet it.)

> Tip: Petting the pixel pet is a nice little pause, but the real one probably wants it more. The free **Attention** routine reminds you to make time for cuddles, and with pet voice reminders it can even arrive in your pet's own bark or meow.

## Fold fun on iPhone Duo, iPad and Mac

PETO is built for iPhone, iPad and Mac, and it has a little trick for big screen changes. On a foldable iPhone (iPhone Duo), in iPad split view or when you maximise a Mac window, a big one-step size change plays a short animation: pixel covers swing open and your pets hop out with hearts. Folding back squashes the app and puffs out paw prints.

It's decorative only, so your routines and reminders stay as they are, and Reduce Motion turns it off.

(Screenshot: Home, where your pixel pets live. Press and hold one to pet it.)

## Dressing up your real pet? Keep it short, comfortable and supervised

A pixel hat costs your pet nothing. A real costume is different, and animal-welfare charities are cautious about it. The PDSA advises avoiding clothes that aren't designed to keep a pet warm or safe, because outfits can get in the way of going to the toilet or grooming and can make a pet too hot. The ASPCA recommends not putting a dog or cat in a costume unless you know they love it.

If you still want a festive photo of your real pet:

- Choose a costume that doesn't limit movement, sight, breathing or the ability to bark or meow, with no small, dangling or easily chewed-off pieces (ASPCA).

- Let your pet try it on before the big day, and keep it on only briefly, for example for a photo (ASPCA, RSPCA Australia).

- Watch for stress. RSPCA Australia mentions panting, lip licking and showing the whites of the eyes; the PDSA adds yawning in dogs and over-grooming, aggression or extra noise in cats. If your pet tries to get it off, take it off.

- Supervise the whole time and never leave a pet in a costume unattended (RSPCA Australia).

- Cats generally don't enjoy being dressed up. A festive bandana for a moment, or no costume at all, is fine (RSPCA Australia, ASPCA).

If your pet seems stressed or unwell afterwards, ask your vet.

## Seasonal outfit checklist

- [ ] Open your pet, then Edit Pet → Outfits
- [ ] Try on Halloween, New Year and Bayram headwear for free
- [ ] Keep your favourite with Premium
- [ ] Press and hold your pixel pet to pet it
- [ ] Look in at night and in the morning to see it sleep and wake
- [ ] Log a walk and look for muddy paws
- [ ] Dressing up your real pet: brief, comfortable, supervised

New to PETO? Start with the quick-start guide.

## Questions people ask

**When can I dress my pet up for Halloween, New Year or Bayram in PETO?** Any time. PETO features Halloween from 1 October to 7 November, New Year from 1 December to 15 January and Bayram from a week before Ramazan Bayramı and Kurban Bayramı, with dates from the Umm al-Qura calendar. Released outfits stay wearable all year.

**Are PETO's seasonal outfits free?** Trying them on is free for everyone. Keeping an outfit on your pet is part of optional PETO Premium, sold as monthly, yearly or lifetime.

**How do I pet my pixel pet in PETO?** Press and hold your pet on Home or on its pet page. A dog wags, a cat or small furry pet purrs, birds and fish flutter and reptiles nuzzle, with haptics that are mirrored on Apple Watch. It's free.

**Why is my pet asleep in PETO?** At night your pixel pet sleeps in a nightcap under a moon, and the first time you look each morning it yawns awake with a sun. It's part of the free living pet. With Reduce Motion on, the looks stay but the movement stops.

**Is it safe to dress up my real pet for Halloween?** Animal-welfare charities are cautious. The ASPCA suggests a costume only if you know your pet loves it, and RSPCA Australia says to keep it brief, supervise closely and never leave a pet in a costume unattended. Watch for stress such as panting or lip licking, and ask your vet if you're unsure.

- PDSA (2022). Is it ok to dress up my pet? https://www.pdsa.org.uk/pet-help-and-advice/looking-after-your-pet/all-pets/is-it-ok-to-dress-up-my-pet
